messages:
mohit (support): FYI FinCorp is hitting repeated 503s when trying to start a Dedicated pool. Customer reports tokens failing on init (HTTP 401). They flagged this as P1 and want an ETA for a fix — pinging product.
elaine (product): thanks. can you paste the exact error and request id? are they on Dedicated reserved capacity or Private deployment?
mohit (support): reserved Dedicated, tenant=fincorp-prod. error snippet:\n```\nHTTP 401 Unauthorized - token expired\nrequest_id=abc123\n```\nCustomer says it started after our rolling deploy yesterday.
lara (sales): heads-up — enterprise contract, monthly commit + SLA. they expect priority handling. if you need me to escalate for emergency access to their environment, I can.
kevin (eng): quick gut check: a 401 at token exchange smells like either KMS rotation or an auth-service change. options: 1) targeted hotpatch to fix routing/token check for that tenant, 2) force-fallback to hosted path for that tenant while we investigate. hotpatch is faster but riskier.
elaine (product): leaning toward a targeted hotfix + canary for that tenant. need rollback plan, QA signoff, and comms. what's the dev/ops effort estimate?
kevin (eng): rough estimate: 1-2 engineers, 24-48h to implement + validate canary. ops ~2-4h to coordinate. fallback (route to hosted) is ~4h work to add flag and test.
olga (qa): I'll need automated smoke tests for token exchange flows and a small perf check. recommend canary on 2 nodes for ~4 hours of monitoring.
elaine (product): decision matrix — SLA impact > potential risk. propose we run a canary hotfix targeted at fincorp-prod. need signoff from eng manager and security before deploy.
kevin (eng): security note: we should NOT relax validation. patch scope will be routing/auth handshake edge-case only. tagging @oliver (sec) for a quick review.
oliver (sec): ok for an expedited review. requirements: preserve validation checks, add log redaction, and ensure audit trail for any temporary flags. cannot disable auth.
lara (sales): I'll prepare the customer comms. suggest: "canary tomorrow, ETA 48h to fix, will provide updates every 12h". okay to commit to that?
mohit (support): linking ticket and logs: https://zendesk/12345 — added the full stack trace and customer contact info.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary window requested 2026-03-22 14:00-18:00 UTC
elaine (product): owners: kevin (eng) to implement; olga (QA) for test signoff; sam (ops/eng-oncall) for rollout. comms: lara + support. runbook: support to toggle feature flag if we see regressions. after successful canary -> cut hotfix release and ship patch to prod.
kevin (eng): will open PR and link here: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/789\nplan:\n1) branch + unit tests\n2) canary deploy scoped to fincorp tenant (feature flag)\n3) monitor logs + error rate + auth metrics\n4) if green, roll-forward + release; if fail, toggle flag to route to hosted fallback and revert change
olga (qa): adding smoke tests to CI and will run manual regression once PR is ready. will publish a quick checklist.
mohit (support): telling customer now: "we plan a targeted canary tomorrow, ETA 48 hours. we'll keep you updated every 12 hours." they acknowledged and will provide additional logs if we need them.
elaine (product): approved. kevin, please proceed and post status updates here. tag #incidents if this escalates. :thumbsup:
kevin (eng): starting work now, will post PR + timeline updates in this thread.
